value.lineage: README: JAX-based reimplementation of the baselines in facebookresearch/dcd ('previous reference implementations, like those in facebookresearch/dcd'); AMaze 'provides feature-parity with respect to the previous reference implementation of the maze environment in facebookresearch/dcd' and 'exactly reproduces the MiniGrid-based mazes used in previous UED studies'. Introduces Parallel PLR and Parallel ACCEL as new variants. rnn.py is based on OptimizedLSTMCell from google/jax. Roadmap names JaxMARL and Jumanji as planned integrations. (Downstream, per the jaxued tree, JaxUED credits minimax commit 2ae9e04 for ued_scores and maze mutators.) || main loop (reader, from the code): ExperimentRunner.train loops while train_state.n_updates < n_total_updates, each tick calling the selected runner's run() (jitted, optionally shmap-sharded over devices) which for PLRRunner resets a batch of fresh random levels, asks PLRManager.sample whether to replay (uniform draw < replay_prob and buffer fill >= min_fill_ratio) and if so draws levels from the buffer with a distribution mixing rank-based score weights and staleness (ages), optionally merges new+replay+mutated levels for parallel evaluation, dedupes against the buffer, rolls out the students and computes UED scores (e.g. max_mc) to insert/update buffer entries, performs the PPO gradient update (gated by is_replay under Robust PLR), then under ACCEL mutates the replayed levels with the registered mutator and evaluates the children into the buffer, before the outer loop logs stats to csv/wandb and checkpoints.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: Provide fast, fully-jittable JAX implementations of the key minimax-regret UED baselines (DR, Minimax adversary, PAIRED, Population PAIRED, PLR, Robust PLR, ACCEL) plus two new parallel variants (Parallel PLR, Parallel ACCEL), with multi-device training and a tensorized maze environment (AMaze) reproducing the MiniGrid mazes of prior UED work.

organs.mechanism: rank mode replaces scores by 1/(1+rank) over the whole buffer, masks by filled, raises to 1/temperature and normalises; staleness is ages*filled normalised (falling back to the score distribution); replay = (1-staleness_coef)*score + staleness_coef*staleness; every draw ages all filled levels by 1 and zeroes the drawn one
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the 'equal weight to present levels' fallback is dead code (z forced to 1 before the test)

organs.mechanism: a new level targets the next empty slot, else argmin(replay_dist), and is inserted iff score >= that slot's score (ties replace; jaxued uses strict <); episodes without a done are masked; mutated children carry n_mutations = parent + 1
organs.failure_landscape: by reading (MEDIUM): max_returns is overwritten by the current rollout's max, so the stored value can decrease

organs.mechanism: RELATIVE_REGRET = clip(max_return[agent1] - mean_return[agent0], 0); MEAN_RELATIVE_REGRET mean - mean; POPULATION_REGRET max over agents - mean; L1_VALUE_LOSS mean |advantage| (the PLR default); POSITIVE_VALUE_LOSS mean clip(adv, 0); MAX_MC max(max_return) - value; VALUE_DISAGREEMENT std of values; envs without a done get ignore_val

parallel mode forces replay_prob 1.0 and the batch criterion and evaluates new, replayed and mutated levels in one rollout, taking gradients only from the replay slice; robust PLR skips gradients on non-replay steps; easy/hard mutation criteria pick parents by min/max UED score
